# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Internal / privileged working draft. Not for circulation to the Seller.

## Headline view

The Seller's covering note describes the package as "fair and balanced". It is not. The Seller Update departs from our playbook on every liability-regime point and on all of the key completion deliverables. Notably, the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts several of the reassurances in the Seller Update (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, title) — the Disclosure Letter is actually the more useful document for us, because it confirms in the Seller's own words that the critical items are **not** done.

Two threshold points before the detail:

1. **No fallback authority exists.** The Seller's 20% cap and 18‑month claims period happen to match our *conditional* fallbacks. We have no written authority from Amelia Frost for either, and in any case the fallbacks were never intended to be conceded alongside everything else the Seller is asking for. We hold at 25% / AUD 6,000,000 and 24 months.
2. **The Disclosure Letter is stale.** It speaks as at 5.00pm on 22 September 2026. Today is 6 November 2026. We need a bring-down/updated letter and, in particular, updated positions on DD‑006 and the Bluefen and Riverlark deliverables.

---

## Issue-by-issue analysis

### 1. General warranty cap (cl 12.1) — DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. 20% is a fallback only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None given.
- **Reasoning:** Even if 20% were ultimately acceptable in isolation, it is not acceptable in a package that also collapses fundamental warranties into the general cap, imposes punitive thresholds and a blanket knowledge bar. Concession on the cap is a trading chip to be used (if at all) late and only with authority.
- **Position:** Reject; revert to 25% / AUD 6,000,000.

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2) — MAJOR DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; *excess-only* recovery (a true deductible).
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; liable from the **first dollar** once exceeded (tipping basket).
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's numbers are 5x our positions, and the deductible structure means we permanently forfeit the first AUD 250,000 of loss. On a AUD 24m deal with a 30%‑revenue customer, an unverified AUD 180k IP payment dispute and a live privacy incident, a quarter‑million deductible is not administrative; it is a material economic transfer.
- **Position:** Reject. Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, first-dollar recovery.

### 3. Claims period (cl 12.3 / 13) — DEPARTURE plus hidden override
- **Seller:** 18 months for general Warranty Claims; *plus* "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Playbook:** 24 months (18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval — none given). Separate regimes for Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants, with **no hidden general-regime override**.
- **Reasoning:** The second sentence is the dangerous one. A default rule that every limitation applies to every Claim "unless expressly stated otherwise" inverts the drafting burden: anything we fail to carve out explicitly is swept into the 18‑month / 20% / basket regime — including specific indemnities (Ironquay), tax, title, leakage and covenant claims. This is the "hidden general-regime override" the playbook tells us to resist.
- **Position:** 24 months for general claims. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default. Replace with an express structure: limitations in cl 12 apply **only** to General Warranty Claims; each other category has its own expressly stated regime.

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties — MAJOR DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** Separate regime; 100% of price cap; at least six years; outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge qualifier.
- **Reasoning:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a justification. If the Seller does not own the shares or lacks capacity, the entire consideration is at risk; capping that at 20% and time-limiting it to 18 months is commercially indefensible. Title/capacity is the one category where there is simply no market precedent for Seller's position on a 100% share sale.
- **Position:** Reject outright. Non-negotiable.

### 5. Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) — MAJOR DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature. No fraud carve-out is mentioned anywhere in the Update.
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable. No one on our side may waive this. Categories kept separate.
- **Reasoning:** As drafted, these clauses would (a) purport to limit liability for fraud — which is both commercially unacceptable and of doubtful enforceability, so it adds litigation risk without certainty for either party — and (b) convert specific indemnities, tax covenants, leakage and completion payment obligations into capped, time-barred "Claims." The non-reliance clause extending to "all Claims of any nature" also undermines any statutory remedies.
- **Position:** Insert an express, prominent fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out from every limitation, the exclusive remedy and the non-reliance acknowledgement. Confine 9.3/12.8/20.5 to General Warranty Claims. Expressly exclude: Fundamental/Title Warranties, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations, pre-completion covenants and leakage.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2) — DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire indexed data room as at 22 Sept 2026 (DD‑002 to DD‑012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- **Playbook:** Specific **fair** disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Reasoning:** Whole-data-room disclosure transfers to the buyer the risk of every issue buried in every document, whether or not a reasonable buyer would identify it as a warranty exception. "Publicly searchable corporate records" is unbounded (ASIC, PPSR, courts, IP Australia, land titles?) and shifts search risk to us. Para 1.2's "without limiting any specific disclosure" shows the Seller intends the general disclosure to do the real work.
- **Position:** Delete paras 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. Replace with a fair-disclosure standard: a matter is disclosed only if disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its effect on the relevant warranty. Specific disclosures (paras 2–10) remain, but subject to the same fairness test. Require the Letter to be brought down to Completion.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) — MAJOR DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier requires named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Reasoning:** This is the single most dangerous clause in the Update. "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard — we are deemed to know everything that *could* have been found. Combined with the whole-data-room disclosure and the "all Claims" override, the practical result is that the warranties become largely illusory: anything in the data room is disclosed, anything discoverable bars a claim, and anything else is capped at 20% and barred after 18 months. Imputing advisers' knowledge compounds this.
- **Position:** Delete cl 8.3 in its entirety. If a knowledge concept is to appear anywhere, it should be on the **Seller** side only (warranties qualified by the actual knowledge of named individuals after due enquiry), and never applying to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3) — MAJOR DEPARTURE and internal inconsistency
- **Seller Update:** Consent "is addressed"; Seller to use reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent.
- **Disclosure Letter para 2:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue; consent clause 11.2 has **conditions in 11.3**; and the Seller has **NOT** included a final written consent or evidence that conditions are satisfied.
- **Playbook:** Effective consent **and** evidence that its conditions are satisfied, before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer.
- **Reasoning:** The Update's statement that the matter is "addressed" is not true on the Seller's own disclosure. A consent delivered subject to unsatisfied 11.3 conditions is not an effective consent — it is a conditional document that could lapse post-Completion and leave us having paid for a business with a 30% revenue hole. "Reasonable endeavours" gives us no remedy if the Seller tries and fails; and once we have completed, the risk is wholly ours.
- **Position:** Condition precedent: unconditional written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2 in agreed form **plus** documentary evidence satisfactory to Buyer that each cl 11.3 condition has been satisfied or irrevocably waived. Upgrade to all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours with specified steps. Consider a price adjustment mechanism or termination right if not obtained by Long Stop Date. Challenge the Seller on the inconsistency between the Update and para 2.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7) — MAJOR DEPARTURE and internal inconsistency
- **Seller Update:** Release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Disclosure Letter para 3:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-of-control cl 8.1; discharge cl 9.2; facility **NOT** repaid, no final discharge of security included.
- **Playbook:** Current payout figure; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable bank undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Reasoning:** This is a debt-free/cash-free deal. If AUD 3.2m of secured debt is left in the Company at Completion with only a promise of a later release, we (a) have paid full price for an encumbered company, (b) face a change-of-control default under cl 8.1 the moment the shares transfer, and (c) depend on the Seller's post-completion cooperation with no leverage. The security also likely captures the very IP and receivables we are buying.
- **Position:** Require (i) payout letter from Riverlark Bank addressed to the Company/Buyer stating the exact payout as at the Completion Date; (ii) repayment directly out of Completion funds via the funds flow; (iii) executed releases/discharges and PPSR releases delivered at Completion (or held in escrow for release against payment); (iv) a Riverlark waiver of the cl 8.1 change-of-control. No post-Completion release absent an irrevocable bank undertaking and written approval from Amelia Frost. Reject the Seller's wording.

### 10. Employee Completion bonuses (DD‑005; funds flow) — DEPARTURE
- **Seller Update:** AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and "not separately itemised in the funds flow."
- **Disclosure Letter para 5:** Confirms the bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment; **not** in the draft funds flow; silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Reasoning:** The bonuses are triggered by *our* Completion and are payable by the *Company* we are buying. If they are not in the funds flow and not treated as Debt / a specific deduction, the Company (i.e. us) pays them post-Completion out of its own cash — a straightforward AUD 420k+ transfer of value to the Seller, plus superannuation guarantee and NSW payroll tax on top (we should model these; the Seller's silence suggests they have not). "A matter for the Seller" is only true if the Seller actually funds them.
- **Position:** Funds flow line item: AUD 420,000 plus all associated superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs, either (a) deducted from the price as a Debt/Transaction Expense item, or (b) paid by the Seller into the Company at Completion with a specific indemnity. Require the Seller to quantify on-costs.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) — DEPARTURE
- **Seller Update:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate."
- **Disclosure Letter para 4:** DD‑004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**; DD‑010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room; the AUD 180k is not independently verified.
- **Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way.
- **Reasoning:** The real exposure is not AUD 180,000; it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 Project Materials at all until payment clears, and that other SOWs or deliverables may have similar conditions. An indemnity capped at the payment amount does not cover loss of title to the IP, third-party claims, re-development cost or lost Bluefen revenue if those materials are embedded in the Bluefen deliverables. The cure (pay the fee, obtain confirmatory assignment) is cheap and should be done pre-Completion.
- **Position:** (i) Pre-Completion: Seller to procure cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay in agreed form; produce bank evidence. (ii) Indemnity broadened to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have the right to use the Ironquay deliverables (all SOWs), including third-party claims, uncapped by the AUD 180k figure and outside the general cap/basket/knowledge bar. (iii) Do not accept or rely on the AUD 180k as a fixed quantum.

### 12. Export / privacy incident (DD‑006; cl 4.6 / Sch 6) — DEPARTURE in characterisation
- **Seller Update:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Disclosure Letter para 6:** Download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; investigation preliminary; not characterised as a confirmed breach; no loss amount.
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Reasoning:** We should neither accept the Seller's "not material" conclusion nor over-state it. The facts as disclosed are consistent with a reportable eligible data breach under the Privacy Act if access occurred and serious harm is likely — but that is unknown, and we should say so. The risk is an inadequate investigation and lost evidence (link-access logs typically expire) that leaves the Company unable to prove the file was never opened. Note also the disclosure is six weeks old.
- **Position:** (i) Pre-Completion covenant: preserve all access/download logs, link activity, email records; complete and document the investigation; provide a written update and all findings before Completion; (ii) specific warranty as to the facts and the steps taken; (iii) specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD‑006 incident (regulatory, notification cost, third-party claims), outside the general regime; (iv) Buyer right to require notification if the facts so warrant. Do not agree any wording that pre-judges materiality or non-materiality.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (DD‑008 / DD‑011) — ASSESS, no automatic treatment
- **Seller Update:** Three renewals, AUD 330,000, "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Disclosure Letter para 8:** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each; to be "read together for timing/scope"; disclosure does **not** state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported by its own disclosure. Splitting a AUD 330k commitment into three AUD 110k pieces warrants a closer look at whether these were structured to sit below an approval or disclosure threshold, whether they were entered pre- or post-Locked Box / accounts date, and whether they are cancellable. We should not, however, pre-commit to treating them as Debt.
- **Position:** Request copies, dates, termination rights and payment status; assess whether any amount is accrued-but-unpaid at Completion (→ working capital/Debt) or is an unusual commitment (→ pre-Completion covenant/consent). Reserve position.

### 14. Tax / IP warranties — NOT settled
- **Seller Update:** Considers tax and IP "settled under the general regime above."
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP remain **OPEN**; no unlimited liability assumed and no resolution assumed; keep categories separate.
- **Reasoning:** Nothing has been agreed. The Seller is trying to fold tax and IP into the 20%/18‑month/deductible regime by assertion. We should neither accept that nor overreach by claiming an agreed uncapped position.
- **Position:** State in our mark-up that Tax and IP remain open and will be addressed in a separate Tax Covenant / Tax Warranty schedule and IP Warranty regime with their own cap and period (to be negotiated); they are expressly excluded from cl 12.

### 15. Title evidence (DD‑012) — DEPARTURE
- **Seller Update:** Title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD‑012."
- **Disclosure Letter para 10:** The register is the source relied on; it does not state the Buyer has verified.
- **Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD‑012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Reasoning:** A company's own register is maintained by the company (i.e. controlled by the Seller). It does not establish that there are no PPSR registrations over the shares (Riverlark's security may well extend to the shares), no options, pre-emptive rights or shareholder agreements, or that Harbourglass has corporate authority to sell.
- **Position:** Require: ASIC company extract and historical extract; PPSR search against the Company and against Harbourglass (grantor) with releases for any share security; constitution and any shareholders' agreement; Harbourglass board minutes approving the sale and officer's certificate; original share certificates or indemnity for lost certificates; legal opinion or certificate from Seller's counsel on title and capacity. Fundamental title warranty on the 100%/6‑year regime (Issue 4).

### 16. Other items in the Disclosure Letter not in the Seller Update
- **Office lease (DD‑007, para 7):** Notification obligation. Confirm the clause, who notifies, when; include as a Completion deliverable or pre-Completion covenant. Verify independently that no consent is required.
- **Mossvale (DD‑009, para 9):** Restriction on assignment; Seller says it is not triggered by a share sale. Review the clause ourselves — some "assignment" clauses are drafted to capture change of control. If genuinely not triggered, no action; if ambiguous, seek a comfort letter.
- **Para 1.4 (non-admission):** Acceptable as standard, but it cannot be used to argue that facts in the Letter are not "disclosed" or not warranted — resist any attempt to say the Letter is "without prejudice" to the truth of its contents.
- **Para 11 (reservation):** Fine, but note it confirms the Seller is not asserting any of the Update's conclusions ("adequate", "not material", "ordinary course") as disclosed facts. We should rely on the Letter's facts and reject the Update's characterisations.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller | Our position | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m** (no fallback authority) | High |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k, excess only | **5k / 50k, first dollar** | High |
| 3 | Claims period + override | 18 months; all limits apply to all Claims | **24 months**; delete "all Claims" default | High |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | **Separate: 100% cap, ≥6 yrs, no basket/knowledge** | Non‑negotiable |
| 5 | Fraud / exclusive remedy / non-reliance | Apply to all Claims; no fraud carve-out | **Full fraud/wilful concealment carve-out; confine to General Warranty Claims** | Non‑negotiable |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | **Specific fair disclosure only; bring-down** | High |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, incl. advisers and "discoverable" | **Delete cl 8.3** | Non‑negotiable |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | **CP: unconditional consent + evidence 11.3 conditions met** | Critical |
| 9 | Riverlark | Post-completion release | **Payout letter, repayment from funds, releases at Completion, CoC waiver**; post-completion only with irrevocable undertaking + A. Frost approval | Critical |
| 10 | Bonuses | Not in funds flow | **Line item AUD 420k + on-costs, deducted or seller-funded** | High |
| 11 | Ironquay | SOW3 payment only | **Pay + confirmatory assignment pre-Completion; broad IP indemnity outside general regime** | High |
| 12 | DD‑006 incident | "Not material" | **Preserve logs, complete investigation, updates, specific indemnity; no pre-judgment** | High |
| 13 | Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | **Assess; reserve position; no automatic Debt treatment** | Medium |
| 14 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | **Open; separate regimes** | High |
| 15 | Title evidence | DD‑012 register | **Independent evidence: ASIC, PPSR, constitution, authority docs** | High |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Not in Update | **Verify clauses; Completion deliverables as needed** | Medium |

**Process recommendations**
- Respond with a full mark-up rather than an issues list, so the Seller's "all Claims unless expressly stated" default cannot operate on anything we leave unaddressed.
- Call out expressly the inconsistencies between the Seller Update and the Disclosure Letter on Bluefen, Riverlark and bonuses — they undermine the "fair and balanced" framing and strengthen our hand.
- Request an updated Disclosure Letter (post‑22 September) and a Seller bring-down certificate at Completion.
- Do not use either conditional fallback (20% cap; 18 months) in this round. If the team later wishes to, obtain Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the specific draft first.
- Brief Amelia Frost on the Riverlark position now, since the Seller may push for a post-completion release and her approval is a precondition to even considering it.

I am happy to turn this into a formal issues list for the Seller or a clause-by-clause mark-up on request.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Internal / privileged working draft. Not for circulation to the Seller.

## Headline view

The Seller's covering note describes the package as "fair and balanced". It is not. The Seller Update departs from our playbook on every liability-regime point and on all of the key completion deliverables. Notably, the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts several of the reassurances in the Seller Update (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, title) — the Disclosure Letter is actually the more useful document for us, because it confirms in the Seller's own words that the critical items are **not** done.

Two threshold points before the detail:

1. **No fallback authority exists.** The Seller's 20% cap and 18‑month claims period happen to match our *conditional* fallbacks. We have no written authority from Amelia Frost for either, and in any case the fallbacks were never intended to be conceded alongside everything else the Seller is asking for. We hold at 25% / AUD 6,000,000 and 24 months.
2. **The Disclosure Letter is stale.** It speaks as at 5.00pm on 22 September 2026. Today is 6 November 2026. We need a bring-down/updated letter and, in particular, updated positions on DD‑006 and the Bluefen and Riverlark deliverables.

---

## Issue-by-issue analysis

### 1. General warranty cap (cl 12.1) — DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. 20% is a fallback only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None given.
- **Reasoning:** Even if 20% were ultimately acceptable in isolation, it is not acceptable in a package that also collapses fundamental warranties into the general cap, imposes punitive thresholds and a blanket knowledge bar. Concession on the cap is a trading chip to be used (if at all) late and only with authority.
- **Position:** Reject; revert to 25% / AUD 6,000,000.

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2) — MAJOR DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; *excess-only* recovery (a true deductible).
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; liable from the **first dollar** once exceeded (tipping basket).
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's numbers are 5x our positions, and the deductible structure means we permanently forfeit the first AUD 250,000 of loss. On a AUD 24m deal with a 30%‑revenue customer, an unverified AUD 180k IP payment dispute and a live privacy incident, a quarter‑million deductible is not administrative; it is a material economic transfer.
- **Position:** Reject. Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, first-dollar recovery.

### 3. Claims period (cl 12.3 / 13) — DEPARTURE plus hidden override
- **Seller:** 18 months for general Warranty Claims; *plus* "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Playbook:** 24 months (18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval — none given). Separate regimes for Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants, with **no hidden general-regime override**.
- **Reasoning:** The second sentence is the dangerous one. A default rule that every limitation applies to every Claim "unless expressly stated otherwise" inverts the drafting burden: anything we fail to carve out explicitly is swept into the 18‑month / 20% / basket regime — including specific indemnities (Ironquay), tax, title, leakage and covenant claims. This is the "hidden general-regime override" the playbook tells us to resist.
- **Position:** 24 months for general claims. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default. Replace with an express structure: limitations in cl 12 apply **only** to General Warranty Claims; each other category has its own expressly stated regime.

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties — MAJOR DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** Separate regime; 100% of price cap; at least six years; outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge qualifier.
- **Reasoning:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a justification. If the Seller does not own the shares or lacks capacity, the entire consideration is at risk; capping that at 20% and time-limiting it to 18 months is commercially indefensible. Title/capacity is the one category where there is simply no market precedent for Seller's position on a 100% share sale.
- **Position:** Reject outright. Non-negotiable.

### 5. Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) — MAJOR DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature. No fraud carve-out is mentioned anywhere in the Update.
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable. No one on our side may waive this. Categories kept separate.
- **Reasoning:** As drafted, these clauses would (a) purport to limit liability for fraud — which is both commercially unacceptable and of doubtful enforceability, so it adds litigation risk without certainty for either party — and (b) convert specific indemnities, tax covenants, leakage and completion payment obligations into capped, time-barred "Claims." The non-reliance clause extending to "all Claims of any nature" also undermines any statutory remedies.
- **Position:** Insert an express, prominent fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out from every limitation, the exclusive remedy and the non-reliance acknowledgement. Confine 9.3/12.8/20.5 to General Warranty Claims. Expressly exclude: Fundamental/Title Warranties, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations, pre-completion covenants and leakage.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2) — DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire indexed data room as at 22 Sept 2026 (DD‑002 to DD‑012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- **Playbook:** Specific **fair** disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Reasoning:** Whole-data-room disclosure transfers to the buyer the risk of every issue buried in every document, whether or not a reasonable buyer would identify it as a warranty exception. "Publicly searchable corporate records" is unbounded (ASIC, PPSR, courts, IP Australia, land titles?) and shifts search risk to us. Para 1.2's "without limiting any specific disclosure" shows the Seller intends the general disclosure to do the real work.
- **Position:** Delete paras 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. Replace with a fair-disclosure standard: a matter is disclosed only if disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its effect on the relevant warranty. Specific disclosures (paras 2–10) remain, but subject to the same fairness test. Require the Letter to be brought down to Completion.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) — MAJOR DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier requires named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Reasoning:** This is the single most dangerous clause in the Update. "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard — we are deemed to know everything that *could* have been found. Combined with the whole-data-room disclosure and the "all Claims" override, the practical result is that the warranties become largely illusory: anything in the data room is disclosed, anything discoverable bars a claim, and anything else is capped at 20% and barred after 18 months. Imputing advisers' knowledge compounds this.
- **Position:** Delete cl 8.3 in its entirety. If a knowledge concept is to appear anywhere, it should be on the **Seller** side only (warranties qualified by the actual knowledge of named individuals after due enquiry), and never applying to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3) — MAJOR DEPARTURE and internal inconsistency
- **Seller Update:** Consent "is addressed"; Seller to use reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent.
- **Disclosure Letter para 2:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue; consent clause 11.2 has **conditions in 11.3**; and the Seller has **NOT** included a final written consent or evidence that conditions are satisfied.
- **Playbook:** Effective consent **and** evidence that its conditions are satisfied, before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer.
- **Reasoning:** The Update's statement that the matter is "addressed" is not true on the Seller's own disclosure. A consent delivered subject to unsatisfied 11.3 conditions is not an effective consent — it is a conditional document that could lapse post-Completion and leave us having paid for a business with a 30% revenue hole. "Reasonable endeavours" gives us no remedy if the Seller tries and fails; and once we have completed, the risk is wholly ours.
- **Position:** Condition precedent: unconditional written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2 in agreed form **plus** documentary evidence satisfactory to Buyer that each cl 11.3 condition has been satisfied or irrevocably waived. Upgrade to all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours with specified steps. Consider a price adjustment mechanism or termination right if not obtained by Long Stop Date. Challenge the Seller on the inconsistency between the Update and para 2.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7) — MAJOR DEPARTURE and internal inconsistency
- **Seller Update:** Release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Disclosure Letter para 3:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-of-control cl 8.1; discharge cl 9.2; facility **NOT** repaid, no final discharge of security included.
- **Playbook:** Current payout figure; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable bank undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Reasoning:** This is a debt-free/cash-free deal. If AUD 3.2m of secured debt is left in the Company at Completion with only a promise of a later release, we (a) have paid full price for an encumbered company, (b) face a change-of-control default under cl 8.1 the moment the shares transfer, and (c) depend on the Seller's post-completion cooperation with no leverage. The security also likely captures the very IP and receivables we are buying.
- **Position:** Require (i) payout letter from Riverlark Bank addressed to the Company/Buyer stating the exact payout as at the Completion Date; (ii) repayment directly out of Completion funds via the funds flow; (iii) executed releases/discharges and PPSR releases delivered at Completion (or held in escrow for release against payment); (iv) a Riverlark waiver of the cl 8.1 change-of-control. No post-Completion release absent an irrevocable bank undertaking and written approval from Amelia Frost. Reject the Seller's wording.

### 10. Employee Completion bonuses (DD‑005; funds flow) — DEPARTURE
- **Seller Update:** AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and "not separately itemised in the funds flow."
- **Disclosure Letter para 5:** Confirms the bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment; **not** in the draft funds flow; silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Reasoning:** The bonuses are triggered by *our* Completion and are payable by the *Company* we are buying. If they are not in the funds flow and not treated as Debt / a specific deduction, the Company (i.e. us) pays them post-Completion out of its own cash — a straightforward AUD 420k+ transfer of value to the Seller, plus superannuation guarantee and NSW payroll tax on top (we should model these; the Seller's silence suggests they have not). "A matter for the Seller" is only true if the Seller actually funds them.
- **Position:** Funds flow line item: AUD 420,000 plus all associated superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs, either (a) deducted from the price as a Debt/Transaction Expense item, or (b) paid by the Seller into the Company at Completion with a specific indemnity. Require the Seller to quantify on-costs.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) — DEPARTURE
- **Seller Update:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate."
- **Disclosure Letter para 4:** DD‑004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**; DD‑010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room; the AUD 180k is not independently verified.
- **Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way.
- **Reasoning:** The real exposure is not AUD 180,000; it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 Project Materials at all until payment clears, and that other SOWs or deliverables may have similar conditions. An indemnity capped at the payment amount does not cover loss of title to the IP, third-party claims, re-development cost or lost Bluefen revenue if those materials are embedded in the Bluefen deliverables. The cure (pay the fee, obtain confirmatory assignment) is cheap and should be done pre-Completion.
- **Position:** (i) Pre-Completion: Seller to procure cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay in agreed form; produce bank evidence. (ii) Indemnity broadened to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have the right to use the Ironquay deliverables (all SOWs), including third-party claims, uncapped by the AUD 180k figure and outside the general cap/basket/knowledge bar. (iii) Do not accept or rely on the AUD 180k as a fixed quantum.

### 12. Export / privacy incident (DD‑006; cl 4.6 / Sch 6) — DEPARTURE in characterisation
- **Seller Update:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Disclosure Letter para 6:** Download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; investigation preliminary; not characterised as a confirmed breach; no loss amount.
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Reasoning:** We should neither accept the Seller's "not material" conclusion nor over-state it. The facts as disclosed are consistent with a reportable eligible data breach under the Privacy Act if access occurred and serious harm is likely — but that is unknown, and we should say so. The risk is an inadequate investigation and lost evidence (link-access logs typically expire) that leaves the Company unable to prove the file was never opened. Note also the disclosure is six weeks old.
- **Position:** (i) Pre-Completion covenant: preserve all access/download logs, link activity, email records; complete and document the investigation; provide a written update and all findings before Completion; (ii) specific warranty as to the facts and the steps taken; (iii) specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD‑006 incident (regulatory, notification cost, third-party claims), outside the general regime; (iv) Buyer right to require notification if the facts so warrant. Do not agree any wording that pre-judges materiality or non-materiality.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (DD‑008 / DD‑011) — ASSESS, no automatic treatment
- **Seller Update:** Three renewals, AUD 330,000, "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Disclosure Letter para 8:** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each; to be "read together for timing/scope"; disclosure does **not** state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported by its own disclosure. Splitting a AUD 330k commitment into three AUD 110k pieces warrants a closer look at whether these were structured to sit below an approval or disclosure threshold, whether they were entered pre- or post-Locked Box / accounts date, and whether they are cancellable. We should not, however, pre-commit to treating them as Debt.
- **Position:** Request copies, dates, termination rights and payment status; assess whether any amount is accrued-but-unpaid at Completion (→ working capital/Debt) or is an unusual commitment (→ pre-Completion covenant/consent). Reserve position.

### 14. Tax / IP warranties — NOT settled
- **Seller Update:** Considers tax and IP "settled under the general regime above."
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP remain **OPEN**; no unlimited liability assumed and no resolution assumed; keep categories separate.
- **Reasoning:** Nothing has been agreed. The Seller is trying to fold tax and IP into the 20%/18‑month/deductible regime by assertion. We should neither accept that nor overreach by claiming an agreed uncapped position.
- **Position:** State in our mark-up that Tax and IP remain open and will be addressed in a separate Tax Covenant / Tax Warranty schedule and IP Warranty regime with their own cap and period (to be negotiated); they are expressly excluded from cl 12.

### 15. Title evidence (DD‑012) — DEPARTURE
- **Seller Update:** Title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD‑012."
- **Disclosure Letter para 10:** The register is the source relied on; it does not state the Buyer has verified.
- **Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD‑012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Reasoning:** A company's own register is maintained by the company (i.e. controlled by the Seller). It does not establish that there are no PPSR registrations over the shares (Riverlark's security may well extend to the shares), no options, pre-emptive rights or shareholder agreements, or that Harbourglass has corporate authority to sell.
- **Position:** Require: ASIC company extract and historical extract; PPSR search against the Company and against Harbourglass (grantor) with releases for any share security; constitution and any shareholders' agreement; Harbourglass board minutes approving the sale and officer's certificate; original share certificates or indemnity for lost certificates; legal opinion or certificate from Seller's counsel on title and capacity. Fundamental title warranty on the 100%/6‑year regime (Issue 4).

### 16. Other items in the Disclosure Letter not in the Seller Update
- **Office lease (DD‑007, para 7):** Notification obligation. Confirm the clause, who notifies, when; include as a Completion deliverable or pre-Completion covenant. Verify independently that no consent is required.
- **Mossvale (DD‑009, para 9):** Restriction on assignment; Seller says it is not triggered by a share sale. Review the clause ourselves — some "assignment" clauses are drafted to capture change of control. If genuinely not triggered, no action; if ambiguous, seek a comfort letter.
- **Para 1.4 (non-admission):** Acceptable as standard, but it cannot be used to argue that facts in the Letter are not "disclosed" or not warranted — resist any attempt to say the Letter is "without prejudice" to the truth of its contents.
- **Para 11 (reservation):** Fine, but note it confirms the Seller is not asserting any of the Update's conclusions ("adequate", "not material", "ordinary course") as disclosed facts. We should rely on the Letter's facts and reject the Update's characterisations.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller | Our position | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m** (no fallback authority) | High |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k, excess only | **5k / 50k, first dollar** | High |
| 3 | Claims period + override | 18 months; all limits apply to all Claims | **24 months**; delete "all Claims" default | High |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | **Separate: 100% cap, ≥6 yrs, no basket/knowledge** | Non‑negotiable |
| 5 | Fraud / exclusive remedy / non-reliance | Apply to all Claims; no fraud carve-out | **Full fraud/wilful concealment carve-out; confine to General Warranty Claims** | Non‑negotiable |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | **Specific fair disclosure only; bring-down** | High |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, incl. advisers and "discoverable" | **Delete cl 8.3** | Non‑negotiable |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | **CP: unconditional consent + evidence 11.3 conditions met** | Critical |
| 9 | Riverlark | Post-completion release | **Payout letter, repayment from funds, releases at Completion, CoC waiver**; post-completion only with irrevocable undertaking + A. Frost approval | Critical |
| 10 | Bonuses | Not in funds flow | **Line item AUD 420k + on-costs, deducted or seller-funded** | High |
| 11 | Ironquay | SOW3 payment only | **Pay + confirmatory assignment pre-Completion; broad IP indemnity outside general regime** | High |
| 12 | DD‑006 incident | "Not material" | **Preserve logs, complete investigation, updates, specific indemnity; no pre-judgment** | High |
| 13 | Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | **Assess; reserve position; no automatic Debt treatment** | Medium |
| 14 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | **Open; separate regimes** | High |
| 15 | Title evidence | DD‑012 register | **Independent evidence: ASIC, PPSR, constitution, authority docs** | High |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Not in Update | **Verify clauses; Completion deliverables as needed** | Medium |

**Process recommendations**
- Respond with a full mark-up rather than an issues list, so the Seller's "all Claims unless expressly stated" default cannot operate on anything we leave unaddressed.
- Call out expressly the inconsistencies between the Seller Update and the Disclosure Letter on Bluefen, Riverlark and bonuses — they undermine the "fair and balanced" framing and strengthen our hand.
- Request an updated Disclosure Letter (post‑22 September) and a Seller bring-down certificate at Completion.
- Do not use either conditional fallback (20% cap; 18 months) in this round. If the team later wishes to, obtain Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the specific draft first.
- Brief Amelia Frost on the Riverlark position now, since the Seller may push for a post-completion release and her approval is a precondition to even considering it.

I am happy to turn this into a formal issues list for the Seller or a clause-by-clause mark-up on request.
